text:
Sophia: Heads-up — starting a quick handoff to collect runtime/infra inputs for the per-model/route SLO dashboards we need to land this sprint. Targets: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT (time-to-first-token), tokens/sec. Need: metric names, label/tag conventions, sampling rules, bucket design, and any cardinality risks. cc @Emily @Raj

Emily: We already ingest a few things: `app_request_latency_ms_bucket` (labels: model, route, variant, region, capacity_pool) and `tokens_emitted_total`. TTFT currently emitted as `time_to_first_token_ms` but we also have a histogram `time_to_first_token_ms_bucket`. Important: runtime currently drops `model` label for cached hits — that will bias Pxx down.

Raj: Tagging notes: prefer a canonical `route_id` (stable, low-card) + `route` (human name) for dashboards. Avoid `user_id` or request-scoped ids in these metrics. For sampling: runtime emits 1:10 sampling for cheap requests; we should expose `sample_rate` label so we can rescale rates in queries. Also recommend biased sampling (keep full traces for >500ms).

David: Console constraints: panels expect 10s/30s resolution. For reliable P95/P99 we need adequate histogram bucket coverage above 2s — current buckets cluster <500ms. Can runtime add larger buckets? Also prefer `le` semantics compatible with Prom histograms.

Kai: Yes, we can add buckets at 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s. We'll also add a `sample_rate` label to sampled metrics and stop dropping `model` on cache=true responses (we'll emit `cached=\"true\"` for hits). ETA: code change + canary next week.

Sophia: Nice. For the dashboard panels I'm proposing these example PromQL queries (console-compatible):

```
# P95 latency (ms) per model+route over 5m
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(app_request_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route))

# TTFT median (ms) per route over 5m
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(time_to_first_token_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route))

# tokens/sec per model+route smoothed 1m
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model, route)
```

Emily: A couple of tweaks: use `sum(rate(...)[5m])` for histograms to stabilize; add `without(instance)`/`by(model,route)` where appropriate to avoid per-instance noise. For tokens/sec we should annotate panels with `capacity_pool` and `region` to reason about cross-pool routing. Also prefer `1m` for tokens/sec to smooth spikes.

Raj: Agreed. Also call out cardinality limits: dashboards will roll up by `model` x `route` x `region` x `capacity_pool` x `variant` — that's potentially large. We should limit `variant` only for debugging panels and keep SLOs rolled up by `model,route,region`.

David: Ownership proposal: runtime (Kai) owns metric shapes + rollout, eng-platform (Emily) owns dashboard JSON + panel queries, console team (me) owns rendering + UX bits (drilldowns, timepicker defaults). Sophia will coordinate. Can we align on delivery dates?

Kai: Runtime changes targeted for next Tues (1935200000) for canary, full rollout Wed. Will emit new buckets and `sample_rate` label.

Emily: I'll draft the dashboard JSON and example panel configs by EOD Friday (1935160000). Will pin the panel IDs so runtime can add annotations for schema changes.

Sophia: OK owners set. Quick checklist: 
- [ ] Kai: add buckets, `sample_rate`, stop stripping `model` on cache hits
- [ ] Runtime: add `cached=true` label on cache hits
- [ ] Emily: draft dashboard JSON (panels for P50/P95/P99, TTFT, tokens/sec)
- [ ] David: console UX for drilldown + default time ranges
- [ ] Raj: confirm rollup cardinality and product acceptance criteria

Raj: I'll prepare example acceptance criteria: P95 latency panel must have <5% variance week-over-week for stable workloads; TTFT median must be tracked separately for cold vs cached.

deployment-bot: CI pipeline triggered for runtime changes (build #4287).

Sophia: Thanks all — I'll capture notes in the SLO dashboard RFC and tag related PRs. If you hit blockers ping me in this thread. :wave:
